Anne Carson translated the surviving work of the ancient Greek lyric poet Sappho in the acclaimed bilingual book If Not, Winter: Fragments of Sappho, first published by Alfred A. Knopf in 2002. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVWIhtjPb5ak-stOlrlQkzKYJcdUERcUuWp14OkAh6oJugmiS0pv9ObIGlxRNVEbQpKm4XgllztT7V2tVxqamzeE8qWa5fZgLceKhgpS3AzbqHQWtikBRS17YA9e1SCZA), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHrOzAVYo85ARu_FQW5dIe2cAsVkfdMiiSfdkcLQllDkhuB-_mB91mzIic635qvYlHIzdOrpCy-jWFmY9-hbfQ3LfUhNduIKsk5o9pqPIAUC-IPTK_G3mE2hONO7qH6Q0l7DCi3ZvE2zr_8Bw)]
Key Details of the Work

* The Translation: Carson includes all of Sappho's extant fragments alongside the original ancient Greek text (based on Eva-Maria Voigt’s scholarly edition). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHrOzAVcdTpSY6Mw4ppJ0D-_v1tnlPPofQrINByQFl4TFik8y-4a5404EpRzTAWeyA3PRe4WLPit3xF4O20QTq0_TPo3LdDfU590O-DKZvvoFTofFeVODOaJY7KZ6BkyW7pz145kAgnu3lUeM1fW6I), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVWIhtjPb5ak-stOlrlQkzKYJcdUERcUuWp14OkAh6oJugmiS0pv9ObIGlxRNVEbQpKm4XgllztT7V2tVxqamzeE8qWa5fZgLceKhgpS3AzbqHQWtikBRS17YA9e1SCZA)]
* Form and Style: Because only one of Sappho's original nine books of lyrics survived completely, Carson uses brackets, gaps, and white space on the page to visually represent the missing papyrus text. [[1](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:14304040276582430840,catalogid:8402882877546941078,gpcid:6133049941489313444,mid:576462226964519332&ibp=oshop), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHrOzAVcdTpSY6Mw4ppJ0D-_v1tnlPPofQrINByQFl4TFik8y-4a5404EpRzTAWeyA3PRe4WLPit3xF4O20QTq0_TPo3LdDfU590O-DKZvvoFTofFeVODOaJY7KZ6BkyW7pz145kAgnu3lUeM1fW6I)]
* Carson’s Philosophy: Carson described her minimalist approach by noting, "I like to think that, the more I stand out of the way, the more Sappho shows through". [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHrOzAVcdTpSY6Mw4ppJ0D-_v1tnlPPofQrINByQFl4TFik8y-4a5404EpRzTAWeyA3PRe4WLPit3xF4O20QTq0_TPo3LdDfU590O-DKZvvoFTofFeVODOaJY7KZ6BkyW7pz145kAgnu3lUeM1fW6I), [2](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:14304040276582430840,catalogid:8402882877546941078,gpcid:6133049941489313444,mid:576462226964519332&ibp=oshop)]
* Themes: The fragments capture Sappho's deep explorations of romantic desire, jealousy, longing, the goddess Aphrodite, and relationships with companions and her daughter Kleis. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHrOzAVcdTpSY6Mw4ppJ0D-_v1tnlPPofQrINByQFl4TFik8y-4a5404EpRzTAWeyA3PRe4WLPit3xF4O20QTq0_TPo3LdDfU590O-DKZvvoFTofFeVODOaJY7KZ6BkyW7pz145kAgnu3lUeM1fW6I), [2](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:14304040276582430840,catalogid:8402882877546941078,gpcid:6133049941489313444,mid:576462226964519332&ibp=oshop)]
* Famous Pieces: The collection features iconic fragments such as [Fragment 1 ("Deathless Aphrodite of the spangled mind")](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHrOzAVe8JohjMw3f3RrBD_ZoDm1_GUp7IGPLlOoKdKyfHHd3W7euI0mhhxd1eVFIBQHOySdqNs8yPpf4dPJdZfTWUE8KC5irlTNMt-9SGkkNvaWUcBVxsF1F_STLT5UMNa1u5_GlywUd-3ZsL_1je1rlFMHsV99NKa19M) and [Fragment 31 ("He seems to me equal to gods")](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHrOzAVD_WLdsj7ZmEJ9OWEWrrVepLFwBEBO5URomUjDvY1rIJuz6WTekUs-Ks5zU-sudwYlqcYnBiNpz-Ld3Dq12g57yt7bNtU3DnnvrSF2yDfw7nOMXP-JSWABvHxar_ZNPkfHV4CRJq17YjTJRFh0zNluHCvKtDCfLqhyw).
